ko.executive_summary: The semiconductor industry faces acute talent shortage with demand for one million additional skilled workers by 2030, driving aggressive hiring strategies from major players including SK Hynix, Samsung, Apple/Foxconn, Meta, and OpenAI. Companies are transforming recruitment approaches through campus partnerships, redesigned interview processes focusing on AI talent, and strategic hiring expansion in Asia despite workforce consolidation moves.
key_facts: One million additional skilled workers needed by 2030
SK Hynix and Samsung leveraging company-linked university degrees in South Korea
SK Hynix eliminating cover letters, implementing half-day depth interviews for AI talent
Apple ramping iPhone 18 production with Foxconn hiring surges
Meta accelerating robotics with leadership changes and expanded hiring
OpenAI expanding Asia hiring despite Meta cutting 10% workforce globally

implications.text: Major firms pivoting from traditional application-based hiring to intensive technical interviews and campus recruitment, emphasizing international management expertise alongside technical skills
Asian talent pools (South Korea, rest of Asia) becoming critical battleground with direct campus hiring and company-sponsored degree programs
Companies prioritizing AI talent recruitment with custom hiring methodologies, indicating AI capabilities as differentiator in HPC/datacenter competition
Simultaneous expansion (Apple, OpenAI, Meta robotics) and contraction (Meta 10% cut) suggests selective hiring around AI and robotics while consolidating traditional operations

ko.counterpoint: Meta's 10% global workforce reduction may signal pullback in some areas despite AI investment focus, creating uncertainty around actual net hiring trends.

ko.executive_summary: Custom silicon design is accelerating with Google DeepMind's AlphaChip enabling AI-driven chip design, Broadcom expanding its custom-silicon portfolio, and cloud capex reaching $954 billion annually. China's EVAS startup raised $295 million for RISC-V architecture targeting export-control circumvention, highlighting geopolitical competition in custom chip development.
key_facts: Google DeepMind AlphaChip advancing custom silicon design via AI
Broadcom's custom-silicon business momentum continues despite regulatory scrutiny
Cloud capex projected at $954 billion, signaling strong custom chip demand
EVAS (China) raised $295 million for RISC-V custom architecture
JPMorgan identifies semiconductor pullback as buying opportunity amid cloud investment growth

implications.text: AlphaChip demonstrates feasibility of AI automating custom silicon design workflows, potentially reducing time-to-market and enabling smaller firms to compete
$954 billion cloud capex confirms hyperscalers (Google, Meta, AWS, Azure) as primary custom-silicon drivers, giving Broadcom and similar vendors sustained demand visibility
EVAS RISC-V effort reflects China's strategy to develop indigenous custom architectures evading US export controls, creating parallel custom-silicon ecosystems
JPMorgan's bullish stance on semiconductor fundamentals despite current pullback suggests custom-silicon segment benefiting from cloud capex rebound

ko.counterpoint: Regulatory scrutiny on Broadcom and broader semiconductor trade restrictions may limit custom-silicon IP and technology transfer that currently support ecosystem momentum.

ko.executive_summary: Power infrastructure has emerged as critical bottleneck for foundry expansion as AI and semiconductor demand surge. South Korea's government targets 'carbon-neutral AI superpower' amid power demand potentially tripling, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing dominates with 73% foundry revenue share amplified by AI demand growth, yet faces $200 billion bilateral investment negotiation stalling.
key_facts: TSMC captures 73% of foundry revenue, widened by AI demand
South Korea eyes AI/semiconductor power demand increasing 3x from current levels
Advanced fab construction requires 1.5 years; long-distance transmission lines require up to 10 years
South Korea considering 10 coal-fired plants as backup 'security power' amid NDC targets
Korea-US $200 billion investment agreement stalled over risk allocation and profit-sharing structure

implications.text: 10-year transmission-line lead time creates severe bottleneck relative to 1.5-year fab build cycles, threatening foundry capacity expansion timelines in Korea and other markets
Governments balancing decarbonization with AI power demands, driving retention of fossil-fuel backup capacity ('security power') undermining carbon-neutral pledges
73% foundry revenue share reinforced by AI customers gravitating to proven leading-edge capacity, creating structural barriers to challengers like Samsung and Intel foundry
Korea-US investment stalling over terms and risk (Alaska LNG exposure) signals fragility of transpacific foundry/fab ecosystem deals amid trade tensions

ko.counterpoint: Taiwan's geopolitical exposure and concentration risk may limit upside despite TSMC's current dominance, particularly if US reshoring initiatives gain traction.
